flagged.tx: muri zba kän\rit/ nzuzawe nzefé by\ru/thro a

He came from Komo and
he crossed over (the creek) at Swänze.

only savannah grass.

All the way back.

flagged.tl: Next, we start with the actual design of the gardens,

flagged.tx: watik trikasi masuanema nima zf \rä/ b\rä/
flagged.tl: This is the story about Masu.

flagged.tx: ni zf kar zf \rä/ zf masu manema nzrä\ko/rth masu kar
flagged.tl: This place here is Masu, and that is why they called us Masu people.

flagged.tx: ni masu kar zf n\rä/ zf
flagged.tl: We are the Masu people.

flagged.tx: trikasi fof zwa\ythk/ katan b\rä/ nimame
flagged.tl: The story ends like this.
The people left because,
when they were living here first,
there was no government.

flagged.tx: wati frükakmenzo kabe thwa\m/nzrmo katan karen
flagged.tl: The people used to live in their respective groups in small settlements,
where their respective ancestors had settled.
They were living in this way:
We were here at Masu,

flagged.tx: boba wazi bä\m/nzr nima mifinien akrimogoen nä thwa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: and those other people lived on the other side of the river, for example in Mibini and Akrimogo.

flagged.tx: kar katakatan be\rä/ro nima safsen be\rä/
flagged.tl: There were small settlements like Safés.
Others lived in Kwaikér.
Others lived like this in Mefath.

flagged.tx: wati markai fthé yan\yak/a kwayan kabe fthé yan\yak/a
flagged.tl: When the white man came,
he wanted to bring us together in one place.
So we built larger villages.
The Masu people went to Rouku for good,
likewise those ones from Ŋazäthe, Faremkar, and Démändér.
We came together in one village.
We built one big village, that's Rouku.
Before we were like this, we lived individually.

flagged.tx: ane mrn fä\m/nzr ane mrn fä\m/nzr
flagged.tl: This clan lived over there and that clan lived over there,

flagged.tx: ane mrn fä\m/nzr nimame mrnmenzo nzwa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: and that other clan lived over there. We were staying in the clan.
We saw each other from a distance.
When the white man came,

flagged.tx: baibel buk trikasi fthé än\yak/a fof
flagged.tl: when the gospel came,

flagged.tx: wati bäne naf wn\zä/nza nima yuniti wn\zä/nza
flagged.tl: it also brought whatchamacallit, it brought unity.
That's when we really met up regularly.
We became friends.
That's how we still live today.

flagged.tx: watik anema nimame fof n\rä/ fof
flagged.tl: So that is reason why we live like this,

flagged.tx: näbi kar ennzo bä bna\m/nzr anema zane zf
flagged.tl: why we live in one village.

flagged.tx: kar mä nzenme bada zä\ms/a o
flagged.tl: As for the places where our ancestor had settled (first),
our story man,

flagged.tx: kar anema thu\gathik/wrame näbi karennzo bobo fof nzf\yak/mo
flagged.tl: we have left these places, and instead we moved to one village.

flagged.tx: trikasi mane \rä/ nima komnzo fof \rä/ nima
flagged.tl: This was how the story goes.

flagged.tx: nzenme kar fefe zane zf\rä/ masu
flagged.tl: This is really our place here, Masu,

flagged.tx: nzenme menz mä zä\ms/a zöbthé fefe
flagged.tl: where our ancestor settled down first.

flagged.tx: nä mrn we be\rä/ro nima trikasikaräsü fi we nimäwä e\rä/ro
flagged.tl: Other clans also have their (places) with their stories.
It is just like this!
A happy morning is coming.
The wind is blowing.
The village is looking very good.
Happiness is coming back today.

flagged.tx: zena ezi nze kwa trikasi ŋa\trik/wé bänema
flagged.tl: This morning I will tell a story about

flagged.tx: safak menz mane ya\r/a sagaraaneme ya\r/a garaita sagara
flagged.tl: As for the Saratoga man, he was the Sangaras' story man, the Sangaras from Garaita.

flagged.tx: faikore menz mayawaaneme ya\r/a masuen mayawaaneme
flagged.tl: The Bushfowl man was the Mayawas' story man, the Mayawas from Masu.
The story that is coming,
that I will tell,
comes from the ancestors.

flagged.tx: nzone ŋafen bäin ane trikasi ya\trik/wath
flagged.tl: They told that story to my father Bäi,
and my father Bäi told me the story.
He was talking like this: “This is the place here.
The saratoga fishlings were inside here.
Those two were fighting right here.
The stone bridge at Kanathér,
that was time when they destroyed it.

flagged.tx: wm mane sf\rä/rm boba wazi neba kwa\ritak/wrm
flagged.tl: The stone crossed from one side (of the river) to the other side.”

flagged.tx: wati anema trikasi zena kwa ŋa\trik/wé fof
flagged.tl: Okay, I will tell this story now.
I will start this story now in these morning hours.
There were two men.
Just like I was saying before:
He was living at Kanathér.

flagged.tx: nzone mayawa menz monegsi kabe mane sf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: As for my Mayawa man, who was our protector,
he was feeding bushfowls at Téférisam.
There used to be a stone bridge there.

flagged.tx: wm mane sf\rä/rm neba kwa\ritak/wrm boba wazi
flagged.tl: That stone bridge went across from one side to the other side,
As for that Sangara,

flagged.tx: naf safak fur boba zraen thu\mgthk/wrm kanathren bobafa
flagged.tl: he was feeding Saratoga fishlings there in the swamp, at the Kanathér side.

flagged.tx: okay bänema mane ya\r/a mayawa menz
flagged.tl: Okay, that other one, the Mayawa story man,
who was feeding the bushfowls,
he lived at Téférisam.

flagged.tx: nafane faikore fä fof thu\mgthk/wrm faikore furfur katakatan
flagged.tl: He was feeding the bushfowls there, very small bushfowls.

flagged.tx: wati krsi zn we fä thwa\rn/m edawäaneme
flagged.tl: They had a place for a (fish) trap, one for each.

flagged.tx: safak menz kabe ane mane swa\rä/rm kanathren fä zf\rä/rm fof
flagged.tl: The Saratoga man had his at Kanathér.
He placed his fish basket by the stone bridge.
The fish went inside that whatchamacallit, inside the fish basket.

flagged.tx: tfrisamen mane sf\rä/rm nafane fä gwfiyar we zf\rä/rm fi
flagged.tl: The other man placed his fish basket at Téférisam, but
he wasn't catching big fish.
He was eating only the smaller ones.
It was the one at Kanathér, the Sangara story man,
who was eating the really big ones.

flagged.tx: nä kayé ze\far/ako tfrisamfa faikore menz
flagged.tl: One day, the bushman set off from Téférisam.
As he was making his way,

flagged.tx: fi nafane fä fof krara ymd s\wä/grm
flagged.tl: the (other man's) parrot was sitting above.
He was always talking
like this: “Oh, there is a man coming.”
Get ready! Hide the fish!”
While he was coming, the parrot called out.
When he arrived,

flagged.tx: wati kofä ane mane e\rä/ e\rifthz/a fof safak menzf
flagged.tl: the Saratoga man had hidden the fish already.
(The Bushfowl man asked) “My friend, what is this oven for?”
(The Saratoga man replied:) “No, I made yamcake yesterday.
This is yesterday's oven.”
He deceived him badly.

flagged.tx: nimanzo nomai swa\fiyok/wrm e nomai nomai nomai
flagged.tl: He was doing this to him again and again.

flagged.tx: fam zä\r/a ah nzungathf nzä wa\thug/wr
flagged.tl: (The bushfowl man) thought to himself “Ah, my friend is tricking me

flagged.tx: bänema kam fof e\thn/ be\rä/ kafar kofä kam
flagged.tl: because there were large fish bones lying around.

flagged.tx: wati nä kayé zba kwa tönafa w\yak/
flagged.tl: Next time I will walk along the high ground.”

flagged.tx: wati tönafa mane yan\yak/ nä kayé kanathr
flagged.tl: This time he was coming from the high ground to Kanathér.
He departed from Téferisam (and walked) until he arrived there.
As he was approaching the place,

flagged.tx: wati safak fur ane fof ya\yamg/wa
flagged.tl: he was startled seeing those saratoga fishlings.
(He said) “These are my friend's saratoga fishlings.”

flagged.tx: sre\thkäf/ zraen ane e\fn/za safak fur
flagged.tl: He began to kill those saratoga fishlings there in the swamp.
He finished them off.
He only took one with him.

flagged.tx: krara thrma san\thor/a fafen fi z sa\thor/a fof
flagged.tl: The parrot arrived late, only after he already got there.
He said (to the Saratoga man) “My friend, what oven is this?”
He was speechless. They said nothing at all,

flagged.tx: bänema kofä karo ane fof ya\yamg/wa fof
flagged.tl: because they were surprised about the fish oven.
Anyway, they wrestled each other.
He threw away the saratoga fishling.
(He said) “You have tricked me.

flagged.tx: bukaren ane fof bä safak e\mgthk/wa
flagged.tl: You fed the saratoga fish at your place.”
They pulled each other and hit each other. They were fighting and fighting.

flagged.tx: wati safak menz mane yan\r/a tfrisam
flagged.tl: Next the Saratoga man came to Téférisam, and

flagged.tx: tfrisamen fä fof faikore e\fn/nza e\fn/nza e\fn/nza nezä we näbi sre\faf/o
flagged.tl: now he was killing those bushfowls over there in Téférisam. He also took one
and carried it away.

flagged.tx: nzone bä nima thuwa\fiyok/wrm be\rä/ nagayé fof
flagged.tl: `What are you doing to my children?”
The Bushfowl man got up.

flagged.tx: wm ane fof kanathren bä mane y\thn/
flagged.tl: That stone bridge at Kanathér
that sticks out (of the water) a little bit,
he started destroying it.
The Saratoga man said to his wife:

flagged.tx: ni kra\far/e garaita bobo ŋa\fäniz/ne thfn
flagged.tl: `Let's go to Garaita. We will move to Théfén.”

flagged.tx: wati wm ane bänemr tfotfo sf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: The stone bridge was just about to disappear

flagged.tx: thfn kar fi zä\rit/a safak menz sagarama mane ya\r/a
flagged.tl: when the Saratoga man went across to Théfén, to that Sangara place
and he went down at Garaita.
Nowadays, he stays there at Théfén.
that Bushfowl man,
he was coming back, he returned.
He packed up his belongings at Téférisam
and set off and walked to Masu.
Then he arrived at Masu.

flagged.tx: wati nafane trikasi katan nima zbo zf zwa\ythk/ fof
flagged.tl: Okay, his little story ends right here.

flagged.tx: wati zena anema mane e\rn/ fof
flagged.tl: Okay, that is why these two,
give each other sisters.

flagged.tx: zba nezä ä\ri/throth fäms ŋarer boba nezä än\ri/thrth fäms ŋarer
flagged.tl: They give them (sisters) from here as exchange women and in return they give them to us to be exchanged.
The story ends right here.

flagged.tx: zöbthé kabe mane thwa\m/nzrm kabe yf ane thf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: The people who lived (in Firra) before had names.

flagged.tx: nzone miyatha monme \rä/ manenzo z ŋafeé the\bräkn/ath anenzo n thre\bräkn/é
flagged.tl: I only know the ones my fathers have mentioned. So I will only mention them.
Many people from the Mayawa used to live there.

flagged.tx: mayawa mrmrma o mayawama kafar mane thwa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: They belonged to the Mayawa clan or were elders of the Mayawa.
They were from the Mayawa clan.

flagged.tx: bagu fi tüfrwä thwa\m/nzrm fi baguaneme kafar mane swa\m/nzrm a mawoi
flagged.tl: The Bangu were numerous. One of the Bangu elders who lived there was Mawoi.

flagged.tx: okay ane etha mrn mrmren ane fof thwa\m/nzrm fi kabe tüfr thwa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: Okay, there were a lot of people within these three clans

flagged.tx: ane ebar yam fthé ze\wär/a firraen
flagged.tl: At this time, a headhunt was taking place in Firra.
Those who did this came from Mere.
The ones from Mere
have joined forces with the Wartha people.
Others cames from Nzrari.
Nowadays, they call them Safés people,
including the ones living at Nzrari.
These were the men
who killed the people at Firra.
When that headhunting raid took place,

flagged.tx: nzone ŋafe fthé fof katan fäth sf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: my father was a young baby boy,
he left in the afternoon.

flagged.tx: nima zena zf thrä\kwr/th ebar zan
flagged.tl: He knew that “They will kill them today.”

flagged.tx: nafä fof zen\far/ath zizi fefe fthé efoth kwa\bthak/wrm
flagged.tl: They set off together very late in the afternoon when the sun was going down.

flagged.tx: fi z miyatha zä\kor/a nafanemawä bad yamme
flagged.tl: He had already worked it out with his own magic.

flagged.tx: nima zena kwa zan zbo ŋa\thor/thr kabe kwa zena e\fn/nzrth firraen
flagged.tl: (He thought) something like this: “Today the killing will come here” or “They will kill the people today in Firra.”

flagged.tx: wati srank kma sa\kor/a srank ni kra\far/e
flagged.tl: He tried to tell Srank, “Srank, let's go!”

flagged.tx: srankf ze\nafth/a keke efoth zizi fefe \rä/ nzä kayé wo\rä/ro
flagged.tl: Srank said: “No, it's already late in the day. I'll come tomorrow.”

flagged.tx: wati fi yasi mane ya\r/a fi fefe zen\far/a masu
flagged.tl: Then Yasi really went to Masu.
He thought of the people in Masu,

flagged.tx: karbu ote mane fobo thwa\m/nzrm ane badabada
flagged.tl: Karémbu and Ote, who lived over there, these ancestors.

flagged.tx: wati fi ane fefe zen\far/a ane miyathaen ane zizi
flagged.tl: With this goal in mind, he set off in the afternoon.
The headhunters arrived at night.
They were already blocking the space for the attack.
They surrounded the village and came in at night
and killed them.
As for Srank and his little brother,
they struck him down.
But they did not kill him.
They looked around for the small bamboo with which they wanted to cut his neck.

flagged.tx: z zä\brim/akoth thogr thwa\re/nzrm srank fthé mane ya\r/a yakä
flagged.tl: When they returned to look for the bamboo knife, Srank ran off.
They had already killed his little brother.

flagged.tx: wati srank näbi yasi fam san\r/a yasi yn\brag/wa masu
flagged.tl: Srank thought only of Yasi. He followed Yasi to Masu.

flagged.tx: naf fof zä\trif/a fobo nima firraen z thä\kwr/th
flagged.tl: (On the way) he told everyone: “They have already killed them in Firra.”

flagged.tx: fthé kwan swa\nor/m ŋarsen masuen neba wazifa
flagged.tl: Then he shouted at the river in Masu from the other side.
Yasi said to Karémbu
“Srank is shouting there. Take the canoe for him!
I tried to take him with me yesterday.
These headhunters nearly killed him.”

flagged.tx: wati srank trtha bya\r/a srank ngemär
flagged.tl: So Srank survived, but he didn't leave any children behind.

flagged.tx: ane efoth yföyföen fthé kwan\kwi/rmth foba kwan\fark/wrmth
flagged.tl: Back then, when they ran away and left,

flagged.tx: fobo nä karma thwa\m/nzrm nima safsma
flagged.tl: other people had settled there, for example people from Safés.

flagged.tx: safsma woga nä fobo swa\m/nzrm gfi yf
flagged.tl: There was a man from Safés by the name of Géfi.

flagged.tx: mafanemawä bamu \yé/ thbithé zena mafanemawä e\rä/
flagged.tl: His father was Bamu, but they actually come from Thémbithé.

flagged.tx: fi z zen\far/a ane kayé nima
flagged.tl: (Géfi) he had left already.

flagged.tx: kayé zan zra\rä/ fi z zen\far/a fi anema trtha zena zf e\rä/
flagged.tl: He knew there would be an attack. So he left. That's why they (his children) are still alive.

flagged.tx: fi fthé nya\m/nzrm nafäsü kwa thrä\kwr/mth
flagged.tl: If he had stayed, he would have been killed along with others.

flagged.tx: kabe fobo nä firraen mane e\rä/ra
flagged.tl: The other people in Firra,

flagged.tx: kabe karma mane ä\m/nza fi z thä\kwr/ath fobo nafä thä\thafr/ath
flagged.tl: people from other villages who had lived there, were also killed and mixed with them.

flagged.tx: fi anenzo trtha woga fe\rn/a srank yasi
flagged.tl: Only those two survived, Srank and Yasi.

flagged.tx: yasifa foba fof ni zane zä\wär/ake zena zn\rä/
flagged.tl: We go back to Yasi; from that time until today.

flagged.tx: nzenme ŋafeé be\rn/a nzone ŋafe kwozi maiti
flagged.tl: Our fathers were Kwozi and Maiti.

flagged.tx: fi trtha be\rn/a srank ngemär zä\bth/a
flagged.tl: (This family line) survived, but Srank died later without leaving children.

flagged.tx: ŋare fefe zä\faf/a fi ngemär bana ya\r/a
flagged.tl: He did get married, but the poor chap had no children.

flagged.tx: ausi fäth mä \rä/ra ane zan mrmren nafane yf zafo
flagged.tl: There was another woman in that headhunting raid. Her name was Zafo.

flagged.tx: wati fi mane \rä/ra mathmath gamo zä\zir/a nasi yföen zä\thb/a
flagged.tl: She used magic and hid in the hole of a long yam.
The headhunters simply missed her.
When the headhunters had passed,

flagged.tx: fi fthé fof zän\mätr/a nasi yföfa akrimogo
flagged.tl: she came out of the long yam hole (and ran) to Akrimongo.
She told the Akrimongo people
“They've already killed Mawoi.”

flagged.tx: kafar mane ya\r/a firrama kafar mawoi
flagged.tl: Mawoi was an elder from Firra.
“They've already got Mawoi.”

flagged.tx: wati fobo fof miyatha zä\kor/ath oh firraen z thä\kwr/th
flagged.tl: That's how they found out: “Oh, they killed them in Firra.”

flagged.tx: nezä faw brigsir mane \rä/ra thrmawä e\yak/a
flagged.tl: As for their revenge, that came much later.

flagged.tx: ŋarsen kma thä\thräf/ath fi z zafewä zä\rit/akoth
flagged.tl: They should have stopped the headhunters at the river, but they had already crossed the river.
The woman had heard their names.
Some were talking in Wära language.
Some talked in Wartha and Kánchá.

flagged.tx: wära zokwasi woga nä foba ya\riz/a
flagged.tl: She heard one guy speaking Wära,
a man who prevented the others from killing his sister (saying)

flagged.tx: nafadba ane ausi fäthdba miyatha zokwasi fof za\thor/ath nima
flagged.tl: From this young woman the knowledge spread (and people said)

flagged.tx: okay keke zagr woga zanr thwan\yak/ fi zba z\rä/ safsma woga thwan\yak/ nzrarima
flagged.tl: “Okay, they did not come from far away to kill them. There are from close by, from Safés, from Nzrari.”
Well, the revenge that took place

flagged.tx: nezä faw z w\brig/rnath nzenme aki
flagged.tl: Our grandfathers paid them back
whose (grandson) is now the councillor,

flagged.tx: okay nafa nezä z faw w\brig/rnath
flagged.tl: Okay, they took revenge

flagged.tx: bänema nafanme mayawa kakafar z bramöwä thä\kwr/ath firraen
flagged.tl: because all their Mayawa elders were killed at Firra.
Those cut-off heads would be avenged.

flagged.tx: nezä mane e\rä/ra zagr keke e\yak/a
flagged.tl: They did not go far for their revenge.

flagged.tx: mane n merefo thä\miya/rath nezä faw merema woga kma thrä\kwr/mth
flagged.tl: They were about to go to Mere. They almost took revenge on the people from Mere.
But they decided to turn around and
kill the Safés people at Nzrari.

flagged.tx: krsi znen fobo fof thä\thräf/ath fobo fof thä\kwr/ath
flagged.tl: They surrounded them there and killed them.
That was the revenge.

flagged.tx: ane ebar nimame firraen fof \rä/ra ane
flagged.tl: This is what happened during the Firra headhunt.

flagged.tx: fobafa mane \rä/ fobo fof kerker kwan\bthak/wrm ane fof
flagged.tl: From then on, the hunting raids came to an end.

flagged.tx: monme zane ebarane zan zf\rä/rm fof
flagged.tl: What they did in the headhunt,

flagged.tx: woga thu\fn/nzrmth ebar thwä\rtm/th thf\zä/nzrmth karfo
flagged.tl: they killed the people, cut off their heads and carried them back home.
This incident that was the second last headhunt.

flagged.tx: ane fof \rä/ra last fefe mä zä\rmän/a fethka karen zbo mane thä\kwr/ath
flagged.tl: The very last one, where they killed people, took place at Fethka.

flagged.tx: fethka kar karen fthé thä\kwr/ath näbi fthé fof zä\math/akoth
flagged.tl: When they killed the people of Fethka, the (survivors) ran away forever.

flagged.tx: fobo fof zä\kor/a ebar fobo fof zä\bth/a
flagged.tl: From this point on, headhunting was over.
That is why we are alive today.

flagged.tx: wati zenafa ni tüfr nagayé kwa\ko/nzre
flagged.tl: We are many children now.

flagged.tx: fi ane ebarane zokwasi fthé z maf kra\trik/wro
flagged.tl: But this headhunting story, whoever may tell it,

flagged.tx: zena mrmren fthé niné w\brig/wre näbuné
flagged.tl: when we or others retell it,

flagged.tx: fthé z\mar/wre zane nzenme kar mrmren thd moreheaden
flagged.tl: you just need to look inside our village, in the middle of Morehead.

flagged.tx: nimame krä\nafthm/é thd moreheaden kar mane e\rä/
flagged.tl: I can tell you, in the middle of Morehead, those are the villages (where people came from).
We are not many people,

flagged.tx: bänema nzenme thden ane fof kwa\kwir/m woga finzo finzo kwa\fn/nzrmth
flagged.tl: because this happened in our midst. People killed each other.

flagged.tx: nä kar wogaé nä kar thwä\miyar/th
flagged.tl: One group of villagers attacked other villages,

flagged.tx: nä kar wogaé nä kar woga thwä\miyar/th
flagged.tl: and again another group of villagers attacked other villagers.
Okay, that is what we have done.

flagged.tx: nzenme mrmren nima fof ŋa\kwir/a yam
flagged.tl: This custom was common with us.

flagged.tx: anema kabekaräsü ni n\rä/ra ni mrnmawä n\rä/ra
flagged.tl: We were part of that. We come from that clan.

flagged.tx: firraen mane thä\kwr/ath woga fi fefe zä\bth/ath
flagged.tl: The Firra headhunt really finished off these other clans.

flagged.tx: nafane story nimame firraane fof \rä/ b\rä/
flagged.tl: This is the story about the Firra headhunt.

flagged.tx: nä keke mane fä sa\thfär/a ninzo fefe nznä\thfär/a
flagged.tl: Nobody could escape there, only we could escape.
From Yasi's family to us today.

flagged.tx: nima ni nafane badabadama fof n\rä/
flagged.tl: We go back to his ancestors.

flagged.tx: nzenme mrn mrmren z monme miyatha ŋa\kwir/
flagged.tl: We know about this in our family.

flagged.tx: gadmöwä fi zbo komnzo ä\m/rna karbu ote
flagged.tl: Fortunately, Ote and Karémbu had stayed here.

flagged.tx: firranzo bä bthra\rä/rm mane fthé z thrä\kwr/mth fobo fof
flagged.tl: If they had been there at Firra, they would have been killed too,
and we would not be many people today.

flagged.tx: fi mon zbo ä\m/rna yasif ane fof fam thn\r/a
flagged.tl: Because those two were staying here, Yasi thought of them,
he came back, he ran really.

flagged.tx: fobo fof wa\ythk/ ane zokwasi fof firra ebarma
flagged.tl: The story of the Firra's headhunt ends here.
It is not a long story.
At that time it ended

flagged.tx: nima kerkeren efothen zf\yak/m monwä z nzna\nafthm/é
flagged.tl: in the last days (of headhunting). Like I just told you.
This happened in the last days (of headhunting).

flagged.tx: fthé fefe markai zän\thb/a we mizi zän\thb/ath
flagged.tl: This happened when the white man came and also when the missionaries arrived.
After that, the headhunting ended.

flagged.tx: fthé dibura fathasi thä\thkäf/ath mafa ane woga thu\fn/nzrmth nimame
flagged.tl: They started throwing people in prison who had killed someone.
This story is now over.

flagged.tx: zane namä ezi mrmren nzä kwa trikasi ŋa\trik/wé
flagged.tl: In this nice morning, I will tell the story,

flagged.tx: tdöfien mane thä\kwr/ath kabe ebar mä e\rtmak/wrath fof
flagged.tl: how they killed them at Téndöfi, where they cut off peoples' heads,
and how they took revenge for the attack on Firra village.

flagged.tx: zanr fthé za\thkäf/ath fam fthé w\kur/wath
flagged.tl: They discussed their plans before the revenge attack.
Ote and Yasi did that.
They planned it in Tamnzüfi.

flagged.tx: tamnzüfi mane \rä/ ŋars wazi bä \rä/ forthr fren
flagged.tl: Tamnzüfi lies on the other side of the river in the Fothér forest.

flagged.tx: fä fof fam w\räz/nath faw brigsir bänema
flagged.tl: They agreed on a plan to take revenge on them,

flagged.tx: nafanme kabe zfth firraen mane thä\kwr/ath fof
flagged.tl: to revenge their clan people, who were killed at Firra,
against those who had killed Srank.

flagged.tx: watik fthé wä\fiyok/nath nafa nima zr ŋa\rn/ath mogarkam
flagged.tl: When they did so, they allied themselves with (the people of) Mogarkam.

flagged.tx: kabe zfth fobo nä thwa\m/nzrm fof
flagged.tl: Some of their elders were living there.
Likewise with Fethkakar,
they also allied themselves with them,
So they had formed an alliance at that time.

flagged.tx: watik kabe zba e\yak/a bobo bäne tämnzüfi
flagged.tl: Next the headhunters walked from here to whatchamacallit, to Tämnzüfi.
They gathered there and discussed things,

flagged.tx: monme kwa thrä\kwr/mth fof tdöfien kabe
flagged.tl: how they will attack the people of Téndöfi.

flagged.tx: tdöfien kabe fäth bä mane thwa\m/nzrm fof safsane kabe e\rä/ra
flagged.tl: A few people living in Téndöfi were from Safés.

flagged.tx: mafa zr ŋa\rä/rath firra ebarr fof
flagged.tl: They had formed an alliance in the attack on Firra.

flagged.tx: watik anema fobo fof faw brigsir za\thkäf/ath fof
flagged.tl: This is really why they started the revenge there (in Téndöfi).
So they gathered over there in Tämnzüfi.
They finished (their discussions) and got going.
They went from Tämnzüfi to Sazäthi.
From Sazäthi, they took a shortcut to Térén Zäre.
From Térén Zäre they walked to Käs.
They gathered in Käs

flagged.tx: ŋa\moth/wath kabe yf ane fof e\fath/wath
flagged.tl: and sat closely together calling out the names (of their victims).
They were breaking small sticks,
they broke the stick like this,

flagged.tx: ane kabeane yf nä swä\gar/nzth ane kabeane yf nä swä\gar/nzth
flagged.tl: For this man's name they broke one stick, and for that man's name they broke another stick.

flagged.tx: thä\bth/ath rnzam fobo e\rä/ra fof boba wazi tdöfien thwa\m/nzrm ŋare ngenge kabe
flagged.tl: They did this for as many people as lived on the other side of the river in Téndöfi, for every woman, for the children and for the men.

flagged.tx: nä kabe ya\r/a nzenmema zane karma zf faremma
flagged.tl: But there was one man (amongst the headhunters) who was from our clan, from this village here, from the Farem people.

flagged.tx: safs karä mafä thä\rit/ath fof fi bobo sf\rä/rm tdöfien
flagged.tl: He had exchanged wives with the people from Safés, and (this family) was also there in Téndöfi.

flagged.tx: wati naf thär\kor/a nzone fäms fobo ya\m/nzr
flagged.tl: So he told the others: “My exchange man is staying there.
My exchange woman is also there.
I will go ahead.
I will tell my exchange man (what's coming).”

flagged.tx: ŋarsfa foba za\bram/ako katan bobo b\rä/ro fof
flagged.tl: He followed the riverbank for a short distance,

flagged.tx: watik fobo fof gardar sa\rn/a fof
flagged.tl: Then he called out for the canoe.

flagged.tx: gardar yan\nor/ nafafämsf sren\karis/ oh kabe byan\nor/ gardar
flagged.tl: As he was calling for the canoe, his exchange man heard him (and said) “Oh, someone is calling for the canoe.”
Well, he looked like this,
he was already dressed up wearing his headdress
and he was carrying his bow and arrow.

flagged.tx: nafafäms yan\yak/ fobo fof sre\mar/ fof
flagged.tl: His exchange man came and he looked at him.
He gave him tobacco, really strong tobacco.

flagged.tx: nafafämsf mane thwa\na/thrm zba mane \yak/ako fof
flagged.tl: His exchange man was smoking it first, the one who went from here,
the one who had come for killing them.
Anyway, it was really strong tobacco.
He gave him the tobacco and he puffed it.

flagged.tx: keke naf nima zä\r/a sukufa zane zisé zwa\r/ rma zisé zwa\r/
flagged.tl: But he did not understand (the sign), and (thought) “He gave me this strong tobacco. Why did he give me the strong tobacco?”
Later he was biting his tongue towards him.

flagged.tx: nima ya\fr/tha noku yam w\fä/nza fof
flagged.tl: He bit (on his tongue) in an aggressive way.

flagged.tx: watik nafafäms fam fthé fof zä\r/a nima zan kabe \yé/ zane
flagged.tl: That's when his exchange man understood the message and thought “This is a headhunter.”
They crossed the river there.

flagged.tx: sukufa ä\ri/thr nafathufthnm nafangom karnm ä\m/nzr
flagged.tl: He gave tobacco to his in-laws, to his brothers-in-law and they sat down.

flagged.tx: watik fämsf srä\kor/ fäms fof kra\rifth/e
flagged.tl: Then, his exchange told him, “Let's say goodbye.
I will set off now.”

flagged.tx: nä bana mane e\rä/ra keke thä\trif/a nafafämsf
flagged.tl: As for those other poor guys, his exchange man did not tell them.
Then he left like this,
he crossed the river.

flagged.tx: fi miyatha sf\rä/rm nima zanr zane swan\yak/
flagged.tl: But he knew that this one had come for an attack.
He was spying on the people.
So he told his wife “We are going to leave!”

flagged.tx: watik nafafämsf srä\kor/ watik garda bana kwa srä\rit/é
flagged.tl: The exchange man told him: “I will take the old canoe across and
I will come back the day after tomorrow.”
They said goodbye to each other and his exchange man left.
He went across and met the other headhunters.

flagged.tx: o nima \rä/ nima \rä/ nima \rä/ nima tüfr kabe e\rä/ nima tüfr ŋare e\rä/ ngenge
flagged.tl: (He told tem) “It is like this and like this. There are lots of men, women and children.
My exchange man left already.”

flagged.tx: watik kafar mane sf\rä/rm finzo sa\gathinz/ath mogarkamma
flagged.tl: Okay, there was an old man from Mongarkam. They left only him behind (in the camp).

flagged.tx: kabe naf fr thmthm mane e\rä/ra we nima tätüme thä\nar/nza fof
flagged.tl: He was the one who kept these small branches covered with a coconut shell.

flagged.tx: tätüme thrär\nar/nz watik fi fobo fof swa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: He had to push down the coconut shell. So he stayed behind.

flagged.tx: tätü fof bänema tmod ane ä\fiyok/wa fof
flagged.tl: Using a coconut shell, he bewitched them with this spell.
This action is called tmod.

flagged.tx: keke kwa krä\fänir/ fof kabe gamokarä ane thä\nar/nzath fof
flagged.tl: One cannot move (the coconut shell). It keeps (the victims) suppressed with the spell.

flagged.tx: tätü mä swa\m/nzrm wämne tnz en\thärku/nzath aneme tätü za\nar/nzath fof
flagged.tl: They brought short sticks and used them to secure the coconut shell in place.

flagged.tx: fi bana mane thf\rä/rm boba mane e\rä/ra tdöfien
flagged.tl: As for the poor people there, the ones in Téndöfi,

flagged.tx: komnzo etfth etfthnzo thf\ru/grm yoganai thf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: they simply slept soundly. They were very tired.

flagged.tx: watik fi ŋa\moneg/wath ŋa\moneg/wath e zizi krä\kor/ zzbär
flagged.tl: So the (headhunters) waited and waited until it got late, until dawn.
They sent out their spies first.
They approached from the river
and spied out the village from there.

flagged.tx: o fä e\rä/ fä e\rä/ fä e\rä/
flagged.tl: (They were talking:) “Oh, these ones are there and the other ones are there.”

flagged.tx: anemewä kwa\ritak/wrmth ŋa\ritak/wath zan kabe bramöwä farem
flagged.tl: With this (knowledge) they crossed the river. The whole group of headhunters from the Farem crossed over.
Until everyone was there there.

flagged.tx: kwot kar fthé w\krk/wath w\krk/wath w\krk/wath ktkt zä\kor/a fof
flagged.tl: They blocked and blocked and blocked the village until they had sealed it off completely.
That was when the attack began.

flagged.tx: tä the\thkäf/ath zan e\fn/zath e\fn/zath e\fn/zath e\fn/zath
flagged.tl: Bang Bang Bang Bang. They shot their arrows and began to fight. They killed them and killed them.

flagged.tx: näbi fobo kafar emoth ausi bana \rä/ra fof
flagged.tl: There was one older girl there.
Old man Ote and Yasi chased her.
They chased her down and grabbed her.
“Oh” she tried to tell them “I am your sister.”
(They said) “Oh, we'll take good care of you.
We'll break your neck now!”
They held her tight and pulled out their bamboo knives.
But they did not manage to kill her. They just cut the neck.

flagged.tx: kma zane garsir zf\rn/mth di kam fof
flagged.tl: They tried to break this neck bone here.

flagged.tx: keke ŋa kma bana emoth fäth fä nima kma kwa\frnzg/wrm
flagged.tl: They didn't succeed and the poor girl struggled to free herself.

flagged.tx: anemewä fi nä zan kabe mane e\rä/ra zä e\fn/zath kabe bramöwä
flagged.tl: In the meantime, the other headhunters had killed all the other villagers
and they started to cross the river again.

flagged.tx: finzo fä fof ane kafar emothf thwa\thofik/nm
flagged.tl: Only the big girl was still fighting (with the two men).

flagged.tx: nima zf\zä/nmth kma traksir n zf\rn/mth di kam garsir
flagged.tl: They carried her away and threw her to the ground and tried to break her neck, (when one of them said)

flagged.tx: awkot ngemäku kabe matak e\rä/ z nzn\gathinz/th
flagged.tl: “Oh brother, everyone is gone. They left us behind.”

flagged.tx: w\gathik/nath fobo fof frknzo zwa\nor/m grr kwannzo fobo zwa\nor/m zba mrfa fof
flagged.tl: They left the girl there. She was bleeding badly and gurgling from her throat.

flagged.tx: kra\math/th be\rn/a ai waro kwan thra\rn/ fof
flagged.tl: The two guys ran off. “Hey!” They gave a signal.
The others answered them.
They were on the other side with the canoe.
The others crossed the river (and asked) “What happened?”

flagged.tx: zrkä komnzo z\gathinz/e fof zane bökwan z z\rtm/e katame
flagged.tl: (They replied) “We left her half dead. We cut her throat with the bamboo knife.
She'll just die up there.”

flagged.tx: ŋa\fsi/nzth oh nima tüfr thän\kwr/e tüfrmär thf\rä/ nzenme tüfr thä\kwr/ath
flagged.tl: Then they took stock: “Oh, we killed so and so many of them, not many. But they killed many of us.”
They slept and woke up in the morning.
They rushed off and came to Sazäthi.
Next, they came to Méndüfi.

flagged.tx: fä fof wath thrän\trif/th ebar wath
flagged.tl: This is where they would sing a headhunting song.
“Hey”, the old women and the grandmothers heard them (and said)
“They've already killed them. Now they're coming back singing.”
The women and some older women stood in a row,
and they started jumping up and down holding their fishing nets.

flagged.tx: kre\thkäf/th fi ben\rä/ ebarkarä anemewä thrän\thor/
flagged.tl: The (men) began to approach the village and held the heads

flagged.tx: watik ebar ane fof zzarfo thre\thkäf/th bäne fof thorsi
flagged.tl: and they began to whats-that, to put the heads in the fishing nets.
They took them to the old people and finished (the ritual).

flagged.tx: watik ŋa\msak/wath fof kwa\thwek/wrmth kafar brubru su\fn/zrmth oh
flagged.tl: Then they sat down and enjoyed themselves. They beat the big drum (to let everyone know).
The people heard this (and said)
“They've killed them already.
The Farem people, the Fethka people and the Mongarkam people killed them.”

flagged.tx: watik nezä fobo fof zan w\ythk/a fof
flagged.tl: That was the end of the revenge.

flagged.tx: watik zanma trikasi tdöfien mane thä\kwr/ath faremma
flagged.tl: Well, the headhunting story about those who were killed at Téndöfi by the Farem,
it has come to an end now.
Okay, I'll start talking to you now.
I will start the Nzürna story for you.
The people were living in Yambär.
They slept in Yambär.
There is a creek is at Dimsathak.

flagged.tx: ttfö rsrsir ze\far/ath kabe ausi fäthä
flagged.tl: The men and the women went off for poison root fishing.
There was one man who had two wives.
Her mothers went ahead,

flagged.tx: watik nafaŋafe roukuen bobo komnzo swa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: while the father stayed in Rouku.
The girl followed behind.

flagged.tx: fi nzürna ŋare foba wataya fz masuen zba mane \rä/ kafar
flagged.tl: The Nzürna lived in the big forest of Wataya on the Masu side.
She came this way with her fish net catching fish at the creek,
She was catching those ones.

flagged.tx: wati emoth fäth zba katan z\rä/ro
flagged.tl: The small girl was walking past,
when they saw each other.
The Nzürna called out to her: “Come over!
Come here! The others are already far ahead.
Let's stay here.
We will poison this (creek) right here.”
She was deceiving her badly,
She said to her “You go over there!
Try to chase (the fish) this way!”
She caught them until (the fish net) was full.

flagged.tx: nzürna ŋaref yakme ane thwa\na/thrm kwa\fyu/nzrm mthi
flagged.tl: The Nzürna ate them up quickly. She gulped down the whole fish.
They walked to another bend in the creek.

flagged.tx: we än\mri/nza we gwrr gwrr gwrr
flagged.tl: She caught them and again “nom nom nom” (she swallowed them).

flagged.tx: naf emoth fäthf zre\mar/ ŋame zane keke \rä/
flagged.tl: The little girl looked at her (and thought) “This is not my mother.
This is a Nzürna”

flagged.tx: nima zwa\mäg/wrmo fz zawe kafar fzfo watayafo
flagged.tl: The Nzürna was leading her further into the forest at Wataya.

flagged.tx: watik zrä\kor/ bobo gn\yak/é oh zagrwä
flagged.tl: Then she said “You go a bit further over there!”

flagged.tx: emoth fthé mane w\yak/a ane bobo nä kanzkanzfo
flagged.tl: The girl went to another bend (in the creek).

flagged.tx: bad fä fof gwargwar za\thkäf/a tharisi emoth fäthf
flagged.tl: The girl started digging up the mud in the water.
The water that flowed towards the Nzürna was completely muddy.

flagged.tx: watik emoth fäth mane \rä/ra ŋa\kwir/a moth
flagged.tl: The girl quickly ran off towards the road.
She got there and ran away.
“Father, look at me!
The Nzürna is chasing me. I just caught fish together with the Nzürna.”
Her father ran off and
brought all the people together in the afternoon.
She told them.
Her mothers were still out at the creek,
Well, when the mothers came back,

flagged.tx: nafaŋafaf nä ŋare zrä\kothm/ kofä ya\reg/wr nabi zan nabi zan w\fn/za
flagged.tl: the father chased one wife. She was still carrying the fish. He hit her with the bow.

flagged.tx: we nä zrä\kothm/ nabi zan nabi zan w\fn/zr
flagged.tl: Then he chased the other wife, and he also hit her with the bow.

flagged.tx: emoth fäth ane fof efoth bä sf\rä/rm zizi
flagged.tl: “That little girl (was out alone). It was already getting late in the day.”

flagged.tx: watik nima sizenzo emoth fäth thra\thb/th wawa mnzen
flagged.tl: Then they put two girls of the same age in the yam house

flagged.tx: thäbu e\rak/nath watik e\rdikn/ath watik nima
flagged.tl: They twisted the (girls') hair and tied them together.
They wrapped them up
and covered them with mats and put yams on top.
That's how they left them.
The Nzürna had already arrived. She leaned against the banana tree.
She was watching them from there.
They surrounded the house
while they were dancing:
The Nzürna began to throw fine soil at them.
She made people sleepy.
Until they were done. They fell asleep.
She went and tore open the house.
She went inside and looked at the (two girls).
“Not this one”, she said, “but this is the one.”
She untied their hair and
carried one (of the girls) to the door.

flagged.tx: si zra\mätr/ neba bök neba bök
flagged.tl: (As for the other girl,) she first pulled out one eye and then the other.
Then she pushed her hand in her arse and
pulled out the intestines.
Then she ate her (intestines).
What are you laughing at?
While the people were sleeping, she ate her up.
Then she hung the (remaining) guts on a post.
She only took her head to Wataya.

flagged.tx: watik fä fof ŋa\sog/a warfo nafanemawä mnzen
flagged.tl: Then she climbed inside her own house.

flagged.tx: nafafisf za\mar/a oh bä zane kerere z nŋan\fiyok/wr
flagged.tl: Her husband looked at her (and said), “Oh, what trouble have you been in?
You have eaten a human!”
The husband took off and ran this way.
There is another forest over there.
He was scared and moved away to Tauri Kufak.
The people woke up (and realized) “They are gone!
They only saw the guts hanging from the post.
They choose their best sorcerers.

flagged.tx: za\miyar/ath müsa oh zä zf w\th/kgr
flagged.tl: They went after her (until they found the tree). “Oh, she's in here!”

flagged.tx: watik bthan kwathkwathme wäsi fur y\rä/rath
flagged.tl: Then they wrapped up the wäsi tree with their magic spells.
They piled firewood at the base and burned it.
It burned and burned
and burned and burned.
The Nzürna was looking outside “Oh, there is fire!”
She tried to put out the fire by peeing on it, but that didn't work.
She tried to spray the fire with her shit, but that didn't work either.

flagged.tx: kabe ebar ane fof krän\zir/ mni kma z\fraz/rm keke
flagged.tl: She threw the human skull at the fire to extinguish it, but that didn't work.
She burned completely
with the tree and everything else. Eventually the tree fell.

flagged.tx: watik ane kukakuka kma n za\rn/a
flagged.tl: Well, that kukakuka bird was just about to call out,
when the (sorcerers) grabbed (and burned) it. They ground up the charcoal remains (of her)
until everything was gone.

flagged.tx: zokwasi fof zä\bth/ nzürna trikasi nimame fof \rä/
flagged.tl: The story is finished now. That was the Nzürna story.

flagged.tx: keke nzürna trikasi \rä/ kabe trikasi \rä/ zane kabe fefe
flagged.tl: Infact, it is not a Nzürna story, but a real story.
They later changed it into a Nzürna story.
Okay, it is finished now.

flagged.tx: kabe zokwasi ah nzürna trikasi za\r/ath za\kwthef/ath
flagged.tl: A real story, yes, they made it into a Nzürna story, they changed it.
It is like the (Nzürna story) about Bres.
The Nzürna ate a small girl (just like)

flagged.tx: bres monwä bres monwä zba ya\na/tha
flagged.tl: she ate Bres.

flagged.tx: zane kafar ya\r/a ane katan \rä/ra emoth fäth
flagged.tl: This one was an adult, but she was a small child.

flagged.tx: wataya zba mane \rä/ masu zawe foba fof \rä/nra ane nzürna ŋare
flagged.tl: (It happened) at Wataya here. That Nzürna came from the Masu side.

flagged.tx: zokwasi fefeme na\trik/wé o markai zokwasime
flagged.tl: Should I tell you the story in Komnzo or in English?
I will tell it in Komnzo.

flagged.tx: fthé kabe keke kwot tüfr thf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: there were not many people.

flagged.tx: thwa\m/nzrm zane kafar baden thzé kabe en\rä/ra
flagged.tl: No matter how many people there were on earth, people came here then.
Some people were living in Mogarkam.
Mongarkam is a village.
Okay, others lived in Firra.

flagged.tx: okay nä fä fefe thwa\m/nzrm mänwä kar bramöwä e\rä/
flagged.tl: Still others lived in the places where their respective villages were located.

flagged.tx: firra mrmren mane zf\rä/rm nzürna ŋare bobo zwa\m/nzrm
flagged.tl: Inside Firra, there was a Nzürna, who lived there.
The Nzürna lived together with her husband.
He was a bit of a small guy.

flagged.tx: nafane ŋare nzürna ŋare fof yf mane zf\rä/rm zafo
flagged.tl: As for his wife, that Nzürna's name was Zafo.
They lived together.
Where they really lived was in a Wäsü tree.

flagged.tx: nafanme mnz zf\rä/rm wäsü kafar su\ko/grm
flagged.tl: Their house was inside the big Wäsü tree.
They were inside the hole (at the bottom of the tree).

flagged.tx: boba mnz nafanme zf\rä/rm mä thwa\m/rnm
flagged.tl: That was their house where they lived.

flagged.tx: firra kar mrmren kabe thwa\m/nzrm fobo
flagged.tl: Many other people lived in Firra.
When the people spread out, when they left the village,
or when they stayed overnight somewhere,

flagged.tx: ane nzürna ŋare ausi fof kwän\zinzr/
flagged.tl: that Nzürna took over their place.

flagged.tx: fi zwan\yak/m gatha kar fthé thu\mar/wrm
flagged.tl: She came (to the village). When she saw rubbish lying around,
when the people had left their belongings scattered around and there was rubbish everywhere,
she would grab the broom and sweep the place.
She cleared their house yards.
Sometimes their things were scattered around
and she put everything back in the right order.
She put those things back in the house for them,
(for example) small pieces of firewood.
Then she returned to her own house.
When the people came back again,
the house owners said:

flagged.tx: oh zane ŋare z nzwän\yak/ mnz fath zf nzw\ren/wro z\rä/
flagged.tl: “Oh, this woman was here. She has swept the house yard here.”

flagged.tx: zafe kabe miyatha thf\rä/rm nafanme rzarsi monme zf\rä/rm
flagged.tl: At that time, they knew about their connections to her,

flagged.tx: nafä fi monme nzürna ŋareä kwa\rzar/wrmth
flagged.tl: They were on good terms with the Nzürna.

flagged.tx: keke thu\fn/zrm ane karma kabe naf
flagged.tl: She did not attack the people from the village,

Then got going from there.
On the other side, I called him and called him, but nothing happened.
Then I set off and walked to Fétérsam.
I waited there for some while, but but the dog didn't show up.
I set off again.

I cut a stick for poking (into the hole).
I started digging for the goanna.
I poked into it
and I saw (the goanna) there.
I poked some more.
Then I cut a small bamboo
and tried to stab it.
I stabbed it and the goanna came out.

with this bushknife here.

I cut the small bamboo and

I slinged them and

it is also a funny bit in this story.

and the dogs started (chasing) the pig.
The late mother said to us: “You climb up!”
My big sister lifted up (on the tree).
So she put me up,
She put me up on the zürb tree.
There stood some zürb trees standing on the side.

My sister came down and we walked over
Mother said to us
“Pile up some firewood!

Mum and big sister chopped firewood.
They piled up the fire and we started to burn the pig's hair off.
Mum slaughtered it
and we set off back to the village.

I was as old as Ester there,

we moved back here to this village.

and started hunting a cassowary with her dogs.
The cassowary charged at her and pierced this (leg).
She still had a white scar,
where it wounded her.
When she came back, she was limping.

We left that place.
Mum accompanied us.

flagged.tx: fi nane z za\thb/a bänwä skoroen

flagged.tx: ane nane we z kwosi ya\r/a

flagged.tl: For those workers, their cafeteria and accommodation buildings.

and she did the same in second grade.
They built a house in Kanathér, where we lived.

flagged.tx: nima fefe nzone mane zf\rä/rm zuzir zf\yak/m
